newsitem.title: INDIA: India to offer coal-bed methane projects by end '97.
newsitem.headline: India to offer coal-bed methane projects by end '97.

text.p: India will be inviting bids for exploration and production of coal-bed methane (CBM) by the end of the year, Petroleum Minister Janeshwar Mishra said on Tuesday.
"We are preparing data on the coal blocks being offered for exploration and hope to call for competitive bids within six months," Mishra told a news conference.
He said a model contract will be prepared by the ministry which will form the basis for negotiating and finalising all contracts.

On Saturday, India's Union Cabinet approved a new policy on exploration and production of coal-bed methane which permits private and foreign companies to explore the gas and sell it in the domestic market.

According to the policy, coal beds would be allotted to companies which offer the highest production linked payment. Successful bidders will have to pay royalty of 10 percent -- linked to the value of gas produced -- to India's regional governments.
The duration of the exploration licence will be for 38 years for coal blocks located in normal areas and 40 years for those located in frontier areas.
On discovery of CBM, the companies will be required to pay a commercial discovery bonus of $300,000.
The new fiscal regime exempts the companies from payment of customs duty on import of capital goods for exploration and production.
It also allows foreign and Indian companies to take up to 100 percent equity participation in the projects.

CBM is a hydrocarbon gas recovered from coal seams and is identical to natural gas which contains up to 95 percent methane. However, unlike natural gas, it does not exist as compressed gas and is recovered through dewatering of coal.
